vulnerability.name: CORS Misconfiguration
vulnerability.description: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing configuration vulnerabilities that expose sensitive data
vulnerability.impact: Cross-origin data theft, credential hijacking, or unauthorized API access
vulnerability.mitigation: Use specific origins in CORS policies, avoid wildcards with credentials, validate origins properly

findings.title: CORS Misconfiguration
findings.explanation: The `tx.origin` variable is not properly validated, allowing an attacker to manipulate the origin and potentially access sensitive data.
findings.impact: Cross-origin data theft or credential hijacking.
exploitation_steps: An attacker manipulates the `tx.origin` variable to access sensitive data or hijack credentials.

findings.title: Missing CORS Validation
findings.explanation: The contract does not validate the origin of incoming requests, making it vulnerable to cross-site scripting attacks.
findings.impact: Attacker can inject malicious data into the contract.
findings.execution_path_diagram:
function ETH_VAULT(address _log) { TransferLog = Log(_log); }
function Deposit() public payable { ... }
exploitation_steps: Attacker calls the contract's API with a malicious origin.
findings.exploitation_conditions: Incoming requests do not specify a valid origin.
findings.remediation: Add CORS validation to ensure only expected origins can make requests.

findings.title: CORS Misconfiguration
findings.explanation: The call() function is used without proper CORS validation, allowing an attacker to make requests on behalf of the sender.
findings.impact: Unauthorized API access and potential data theft
findings.execution_path_diagram:
msg.sender.call.value(_weiToWithdraw)(
  require(balances[msg.sender] >= _weiToWithdraw)
  require(_weiToWithdraw <= withdrawalLimit)
  require(now >= lastWithdrawTime[msg.sender] + 1 weeks)
)
exploitation_steps: Attacker sends a POST request to /withdrawFunds with a valid _weiToWithdraw value
Attacker uses the call() function without proper CORS validation
findings.exploitation_conditions: Attacker can reach POST /withdrawFunds while authenticated.
findings.remediation: Use proper CORS validation, such as Access-Control-Allow-Origin: ", allowlisted origins"

chunk_analyses.notes: CORS Misconfiguration vulnerability found in the call() function.

findings.title: Missing CORS validation
findings.explanation: The contract does not validate the origin of requests, allowing any origin to access its functions.
exploitation_steps: An attacker can make a request to the contract's functions without being authenticated.
findings.remediation: Implement CORS validation with specific origins allowed.
